Name: Teleporter Station
Description:
This is a mod of 1×1 teleport buildings. The Wormhole Station links every station of your district into one network, so a beaver can instantly travel to any other teleporter on the map, regardless of distance. The Ring Station works in pairs. One half is built on your paths, and its partner, the Remote Ring Station, is placed free anywhere within 30 tiles, reaching places no path goes. The Wormhole Station unlocks under the Paths build category for 20 Planks, 20 Metal Blocks and 50 Extract, at 5000 science. The Ring Station costs 20 Planks, 20 Metal Blocks and 25 Extract, at 5000 science.

[h1]Using it[/h1]
[list]
[*]At least one teleporter must be directly connected to district paths. The first one placed there assigns the network to that district. After that, the game refuses teleporters on any other district's paths. Every teleporter placed after that joins the network on its own.
[*]Stations run on extract, and are filled by haulers. One extract is drawn every ten crossings, from the teleporter the beaver walks into. The store holds up to 100, and the counter survives saving and loading. An idle network costs nothing.
[*]The panel's Transits row shows how many crossings the store will still cover. When the store hits zero, the teleporter goes dark until extract arrives.
[*]Stations are automatically configured as either local (connected directly to district paths) or remote (only connected to the district through wormhole).
[*]Stations that run low can automatically pull extract through the wormhole siphon. A remote station pulls a batch of 5 extract from the network's designated source. You designate a source from the panel of a local station, with the Enable/Disable wormhole siphon button. A source always keeps 20 in reserve, and only local stations can give.
[*]Any teleporter can be paused from its panel, or with the P key. A paused teleporter's wormhole is off. Nothing moves its extract while it holds, since no beaver crosses, no hauler delivers, and the siphon neither pulls nor gives. Unpausing puts everything back. Levers, timers, and sensors can pause teleporters automatically, like any other building.
[*]Ring Stations work in pairs. Build one on your paths and deliver extract to it. Its panel then offers a button to place the Remote Ring Station, free, anywhere within 30 tiles. The remote needs no paths and no access, so it can sit on an island, a tower, or a cliff.
[*]A pair shares one extract store, held by the built ring. One extract covers ten crossings, and either panel shows the crossings left. Pausing the built ring closes the route at both ends.
[/list]

[h1]The look[/h1]
[list]
[*]The station is a hex-tread metal ring around an eased wood ramp, with hand rails at the entrance. Materials follow the faction, with forged plank ramps for the Iron Teeth and walnut for the Folktails. The models are plain .timbermesh files, generated by tools/make_teleporter.py in the game's own mesh format.
[*]The event horizon takes its color from the network's district. A hash of the district center's nav-mesh node id picks the hue, and it stays stable across saves. Spiral arms swirl through it by way of the game's own Spin node animation.
[*]A dry, disconnected, or paused station hides its horizon and stops the animation. What remains is an inert ring.
[*]The ring plate renders as a dirt path tile with a pale inscription that lights while the route can carry someone. On a crossing, transport rings sweep the traveler and a glowing teardrop carries it across at tubeway speed.
[/list]

[h1]Known issue[/h1]
[list]
[*]Wormhole travel was reworked in 0.4.0. Crossings are now a fixed short flight on every teleporter, and beavers and bots should no longer get stuck mid-crossing.
[/list]
